question.problem: Let $T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7 \\ k\end{aligned}]$  belongs to $\text{Im}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
The vector $v$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T)$ if there exists a vector $u=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]$ such that $T(u)=v.$

Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot u & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7 \\ k\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2x-4y \\ x-3y \\ -x+4y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7 \\ k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y=2 \\ x-3y=7 \\ -x+4y=k.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x=7+3y$, which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-4y & =2 \\ 2(7+3y)-4y & =2 \\ 2y & =-12 \\ y & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =7+3y \\  & =7+3(-6) \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-11$ and $y=-6$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+4y & =k \\ -(-11)+4(-6) & =k \\ k & =-13.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $v\in \text{Im}(T)$ when $k=-13.$
